title: Termwise products of K-injective complexes on a ringed space

from.place: proof, first step, derived-functor comparison after reconstructing the truncation tower

statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Let $T$ be a set, and for each $t\in T$ let $I_t^\bullet$ be a K-injective complex [def-sp-kinjective-bridge]. Assume that the product $I^n=\prod_{t\in T}I_t^n$ exists in $\mathcal A$ for every integer $n$ [def-weil-category-product]. Then the termwise product complex $I^\bullet$ is K-injective and represents the product of the objects $I_t^\bullet$ in $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-category-product].

proof.text: Upstream review #1428 identifies CochainComplex.isKInjective_of_isLimitFan and DerivedCategory.isLimitFanMkQObjOfIsKInjective as the canonical pair; retire the duplicate local conjunction. In this snapshot the canonical source is unavailable. Its three local countable-product callers instead use the available HomotopyCategory.isLimitFanQuotient to obtain the product in the homotopy category, the rightOrthogonal closure under limits and isKInjective_iff_rightOrthogonal for K-injectivity, and IsKInjective.Qh_map_bijective to transfer the universal property to the derived category. Essential surjectivity of Qh pulls back arbitrary cone points; the Hom bijections pull back legs and candidates, and quotientCompQhIso identifies the final cone with Q.mapCone P. These are fully proved local specializations; no new global replacement theorem is added.
